blocks.content: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

rows: Punishes a person for an offense already committed after a trial
Detains a person to prevent them from committing an offense in the near future
Requires a formal judicial trial and conviction by a court
Executed without any judicial trial or conviction by a court
Determined by court sentencing based on statutory laws
Cannot exceed 3 months unless approved by an Advisory Board
Guarantees full right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner
Right to representation is subject to statutory limitations and provisions

items: Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency under Article 359.
Article 19 rights are automatically suspended only when a National Emergency is declared on grounds of war or external aggression, not armed rebellion.
Article 21A was inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, and implemented via the RTE Act, 2009.
Preventive detention without Advisory Board approval cannot exceed 3 months.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 19 guarantees six basic fundamental freedoms exclusively to Indian citizens, subject to reasonable restrictions.
Article 20 provides protection against ex-post-facto criminal laws, double jeopardy, and self-incrimination.
Article 21 guarantees protection of life and personal liberty, which can only be deprived according to procedure established by law.
Article 21A mandates the State to provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years.
Article 22 grants protection against arbitrary arrest and regulates both punitive and preventive detention.
